body_text:
Cayley's theorem. Every group $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of
the symmetric group on its underlying set. The embedding sends $g$
to the bijection $x\mapsto gx$. Thus abstract groups are precisely
groups of permutations, up to isomorphism.
